argument: The named catalog is removable, but the measurement says it is not a single-file deletion, and the consequence surface is larger than a table edit implies. Across the nine supplied chapters I count 80 catalog entries (79 named items plus the Unarmed category) defined at 13 separate table definitions spread over 3 files; 400 source lines that name at least one item, in all 9 of 9 files, with 644 name occurrences in total; 17 chapter crossrefs arriving from outside the equipment chapter, 9 of which are the class starting-kit lines; 9 of the reference chapter's 108 glossary headwords whose only job is to define catalog content; and 6 tables in the reference-sheet chapter that reprint 80 catalog rows, including the Discipline column that gates access by name. Removal also orphans rules whose only consumer is an item rather than a category: all seven weapon properties are defined by named-weapon lists, two of them (Versatile, Loading) by exactly one named weapon; six mount special traits each attach to one named mount; the shield Protection gate exists for three named shields; the donning-time list enumerates all eight named armors; Heavy Weapon rank 3 is demanded only by the Maul; Armor rank 3 only by Plate; and Axes ranks 1 and 2 are demanded only by the named axe rows, which makes Axes the one Discipline whose entire rank surface in these files is named gear. Twenty bestiary lines key a damage or DR number to a named weapon or armor, so removal changes monster math and not only prose, and one encumbrance figure names eight items. My measurement supports the purge as the correct direction, and fixes its price: the yes/no question is answered, but the remediation set is enumerated and non-trivial, and three of the ranks plus the bestiary lines must be settled as a balance decision rather than deleted as decoration. Instrument: two grep-only scripts written to the run directory, findings/_researcher-r1-verify.sh and findings/_researcher-r1-measure3.sh, both re-runnable verbatim by the orchestrator.

evidence.claim: Nine of the glossary's 108 headwords exist to define catalog content rather than general rules, and 14 headword lines name a catalog item. Commands: grep -cE '^\*[^*]+:\*' 21-glossary returns 108; grep -cE '^\*(Armor Weight Class|Versatile|Reach|Thrown|Light|Loading|Two-Handed|Arcane Focus|Holy Symbol):\*' 21-glossary returns 9; filtered headword lines naming an item returns 14.

evidence.claim: Twenty bestiary lines key a number to a named item: 15 per-weapon damage strings and 5 DR strings naming armor or a shield. The monster blocks carry no cards, so the named weapon is the only place the damage figure can live. Commands: grep -cE '^\*(Dagger|Shortsword|Longsword|Greatsword|Handaxe|Battleaxe|Greataxe|Mace|Warhammer|Maul|Spear|Halberd|Shortbow|Longbow|Crossbow):\*' 20-bestiary returns 15; grep -nE 'DR [0-9]+ \((padded|leather|studded leather|chain shirt|breastplate|half plate|chain mail|plate|shield)' 20-bestiary returns 5.

*Greataxe:* 4/6/8 slashing.

evidence.claim: The encumbrance rule's single worked figure names eight items, so the slot arithmetic example is bound to the named catalog. Command: sed -n '257p' 15-equipment | grep -ioE "$W" returns 8.
evidence.quote_or_excerpt: A hero with Brawn +1 has 15 slots. A longsword (1 slot), a backpack (2 slots), a bedroll (2), a waterskin (1), torches (1), a quiver (1), and a dagger (1) is 9 slots.

evidence.claim: Three separate waivers or gates exist only because named items gate access by Discipline: the kit-gear waiver in the equipment chapter, the shield requirement with its kit exception in the armor chapter, and the named entry-requirement paragraph in the disciplines chapter. All three become dead rules if equipment carries no permissions. Commands: grep -nE 'entry requirements|Discipline requirement' 08-disciplines 15-equipment 16-armor-shields.
